title: Bilinear-affine saddle problems with exact scalar values

assumptions.scope: All point pairs in the declared function domain. Blockwise constants are uniform in the remaining fixed variables.
assumptions.description: f=y^TAx-b^Ty;\ \|A\|_2\le C;\ b\text{ has no magnitude bound}

model.parameter_domain_description: $C$: positive real; $R_x$: positive real; $R_y$: positive real; $d$: positive integer; $d_x$: positive integer; $d_y$: positive integer; $\varepsilon$: positive real. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table; additional accuracy and dimension conditions appear in each regime.
description_paragraphs: Assume $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y\times d_x}$ and $\|A\|_{\rm op}\le C$, with no norm bound on $b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$. The two balls $R_x,R_y>0$ are known, compact, and convex. The payoff is affine in each block, so a saddle point exists.

operations.order_convention: This operation is charged according to its explicit input and output, not renamed according to a scalar function's derivative order.

feedback_quality.description: Exact responses from the same hidden object fixed before interaction

operations.coupling: Deterministic exact responses with repeated queries allowed; stochastic sample-reuse permissions are irrelevant.

public_inputs: Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $C$, $R_x$, $R_y$, and $\varepsilon$, together with the stated initial points and feasible-set information. Analytic representations of hidden functions, operators, and matrices are not supplied.
oracle.query_domain_description: all R^{d_x+d_y}; output restricted to X×Y
description_paragraphs: Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $C$, $R_x$, $R_y$, and $\varepsilon$, together with the stated initial points and feasible-set information. Analytic representations of hidden functions, operators, and matrices are not supplied.
Responses are exact noiseless reals, and queries may lie outside the ball. Ball projection uses public geometry and does not supply matrix-vector access.

output.feasibility: output must belong to stated output domain
output.allowed_postprocessing: arbitrary measurable postprocessing; unqueried output permitted unless restriction says otherwise
description_paragraphs: The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

description_paragraphs: This is the exact global saddle-gap expression; it is finite and nonnegative.

resource.precision_model: exact real responses; arithmetic and bit costs uncharged; no finite-bit conclusion
description_paragraphs: Each scalar value costs one $N_{\rm value}$ call.
Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

algorithms.adaptivity: arbitrary measurable adaptive queries and outputs

algorithms.parallelism: sequential; parallel rounds not identified with calls
description_paragraphs: Arbitrary measurable sequential adaptive randomized algorithms are allowed. The private seed is independent of the hidden instance. Queries, stopping, and output may use the full history, without additional span, zero-respecting, communication, or memory restrictions.

guarantees.time_uniformity: fixed target accuracy; not an anytime guarantee
description_paragraphs: A single algorithm is chosen from the public input and must satisfy the guarantee for every fixed admissible instance.

objects.definition: Unknown real-valued payoff function $f:\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_y}\to\mathbb R$.

domains.definition: The sets are $X=R_xB_2^{d_x}$ and $Y=R_yB_2^{d_y}$. They constrain optimization and outputs, not query points.

norms.definition: The Euclidean norm and inner product are $\|v\|_2=(\sum_jv_j^2)^{1/2}$ and $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j u_jv_j$. On the joint space use $\|(x,y)\|_2=(\|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2)^{1/2}$. Matrix norms are the induced spectral norms.
